data.title: Longtime Chipotle (CMG) Bull Downgrades Stock, Warns That Wall Street Is Too Optimistic
data.description: Mexican restaurant chain Chipotle (CMG) received a downgrade from TD Cowen. Four-star analyst Andrew Charles, who is ranked #2,700 out of 12,536 Wall Street analysts, warned that weaker customer demand could hurt sales growth in 2027. Charles lowered his rating from Buy to Hold and reduced his price target by 27% from $44 to $32. He also warned that the stock could fall to $25 in a more pessimistic scenario. The downgrade comes as Chipotle shares have fallen by roughly 24% this year. What is interesting is that Charles has been a long-term bull of CMG stock.

data.title: Why Is AI OKTO Stock (AIOK) Up 176% Today?
data.description:
AI OKTO (AIOK) stock rocketed 176% higher on Friday after the company announced an asset sale and a special dividend. The company started the positive news with the reveal that it has agreed to sell Dream Arrax, a 2015-built 5,000 cbm LPG carrier vessel, for $18 million.

Robin Energy (RBNE) will buy Dream Arrax from AI OKTO, with the deal expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. However, it first has to satisfy customary closing conditions. Investors will also note that Robin Energy is a company that is led by Petros Panagiotidis. Panagiotidis is the chairman and CEO of AI OKTO and Robin Energy.

AIOK Stock Special Dividend

Following the company's Dream Arrax sale reveal, it announced a special dividend for shareholders. AI OKTO will pay a dividend of $3.50 per share via cash or additional shares of AIOK stock. The dividend is payable Nov. 25, 2026, to shareholders on record at the close of business on Nov. 2, 2026.

data.title: Microsoft's MAI-DxO Beats Human Doctors Over Two to One in Diagnoses; Microsoft Stock (NASDAQ:MSFT) Notches Up
data.description:
Remember when everybody used to go on WebMD, and diagnose themselves as having a range of diseases, many of which they did not actually have? Tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) has apparently refined the process of using an artificial intelligence for medical diagnoses to the point where it is twice as good at making diagnoses as human doctors. Microsoft stock gained fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Microsoft has posted a 0.48% loss in its share price over the past year.

It's Never Lupus

Fans of the TV show House will catch that reference right away, but apparently, House's team would have done a lot better if it had the Microsoft AI Diagnostic Orchestrator (MAI-DxO) on its side. Reports note that the tool "substantially outperformed practicing generalist physicians" in terms of overall diagnostic accuracy while ordering fewer tests and procedures on the patients. Naturally, real-world use of such a tool would require clinical testing, but if the early results hold out into the larger tests, then we may be running all our medical diagnoses through AI soon.

Microsoft plans to start testing the system further at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston before the year is out. An early test—the results of which were posted in the New England Journal of Medicine—revealed that the MAI-DxO system had an 83.2% success rate for diagnostic accuracy. Generalist physicians with reference materials, meanwhile, could only pull off a 36.1% accuracy rate. Without the reference materials, that rate plunged to 22%.

It Can't Be That Expensive

Meanwhile, a former Microsoft executive is coming out and saying the projected prices on Project Helix are too high to be believed. Former staffer Mike Ybarra simply cannot swallow the proposition that Microsoft would ever charge between $1,200 and $1,800 for the Project Helix, as earlier reports projected. The biggest reason for his objection is simple: a marked lack of value.

Consoles are "mass-audience devices," Ybarra noted. Thus, they need to be able to reach the mass audience. A price tag like that simply prices out the mass audience. Thus, Ybarra noted, "A console at the prices rumored below will never sell meaningful units to be of any value vs. alternatives. Zero."

data.title: "Project Crystal Sun" Gets Approval in Texas, Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Slips
data.description:
Electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA) managed to get approval for its "Project Crystal Sun" initiative in Texas, as Fort Bend County commissioners offered up a slate of tax benefits for Tesla's planned solar cell factory. This is one of the last local approvals Tesla needed. Tesla will now determine where exactly to build its newest factory. Tesla shares still dropped fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 13.64% loss in its share price over the past year.

Spoiled for Choice

Reports suggest that Tesla would get a property tax abatement out of Fort Bend County, along with what was called a "Chapter 381 economic development agreement." Further, Tesla was in line to get a "…foreign trade zone non-objection," along with payments in lieu of certain taxes and a separate payment in lieu of taxes "true-up" agreement. A true-up is generally the difference between estimated payments—in this case tax payments–and actual payments taxes assessed.

Once the project goes live, Tesla will start building a factory that makes solar cells and finished modules. It is looking to do so on a parcel of land roughly 3,000 acres south of the Brazos River in Texas. The plant will handle every part of the process, starting with raw metal and going all the way through solar cell testing, reports note. The new plan offered does not necessarily mean that area will get the Tesla plant installed. It does increase the chances as Tesla now knows what the local government is willing to offer.

Promotion

Tesla Cameras Save the Day

We all know that Tesla cars come with an array of cameras, but many of us might not have expected Tesla cameras to serve as a way to protect a person against false allegations. This happened to a man named Kevin Finley in Seminole County, Florida, where a Tesla camera recorded video that led to him being found not guilty of charges in court.

Finley had been the subject of a traffic stop where he was alleged to have driven through an intersection at a high rate of speed. While he was never charged with felony fleeing and eluding, he was issued a set of citations for other charges. Finley asserted that he had not done any such thing and had the video to prove it. The officers at the time did not care, reports note. The video did, however, care and ultimately disproved several of the officers' allegations. One of the officers, Officer Erik Schwartz, was ultimately dismissed from his position as part of an investigation into the charges.

data.title: SpaceX's Musk Disputes NASA's 22-Launch Estimate for Moon Landing – 'That's Way Too High'
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk says that his company will need just six to eight Starship launches to prepare for a crewed Moon landing, far fewer than the 22 flights recently estimated by a NASA safety panel member. Former astronaut Charlie Precourt warned that refueling SpaceX's lunar lander could be a major challenge for NASA's Artemis IV mission, which is scheduled to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028. Precourt made the comments during a meeting of NASA's Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel. After Ars Technica reported his estimate, Musk responded on X by saying "that's way too high."

The disagreement is due to a problem with SpaceX's massive Starship rocket. It uses so much fuel to reach Earth's orbit that it needs to refuel before traveling to the Moon.

To solve this, SpaceX plans to launch a special Starship that acts like a gas station in space. Other Starships would then fly into orbit and transfer fuel into the storage vehicle. Once enough fuel has been collected, the lunar lander would refuel and continue toward the Moon.

Promotion

High conviction SPCX bulls now have this Tradr ETF

However, each delivery requires another rocket launch, which explains why the number matters.

Why NASA and Musk Have Different Starship Estimates

One major factor is how much fuel each Starship can carry into orbit. If SpaceX improves the rocket's carrying capacity, fewer trips would be needed to fill the storage vehicle. Another challenge is that Starship uses extremely cold liquid fuel, which slowly evaporates while stored in space. Some fuel could also be lost during transfers between spacecraft. Neither estimate has been proven through a full orbital refueling demonstration.

Nevertheless, SpaceX plans to attempt its first large-scale fuel transfer in early 2027, according to SpacePolicyOnline. NASA also expects an uncrewed Starship Moon landing test to happen toward the end of that year.

Meanwhile, NASA has awarded SpaceX about $4.04 billion through two contracts to develop Starship lunar landers.

data.title: Bloom Energy Stock Is Plunging 11% Today — But Don't Rush to Buy, Says Top Analyst
data.description:
A blowout earnings report was supposed to give Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE) investors something to cheer about, but the market had other ideas. Shares of the power tech company are plunging 11% on Friday, bringing their October losses to a painful 30%. Despite the strong quarterly results, investors appear far more concerned about how much they're paying for the company's future growth than how well it performed in the latest quarter.

The company reported third-quarter revenue of $1.24 billion, beating analysts' expectations of $1.06 billion. Adjusted earnings of $0.94 per share likewise exceeded estimates of $0.68, while Bloom raised its full-year sales forecast to between $4.4 billion and $4.6 billion.

Great results indeed, but they were overshadowed by sky-high expectations, concerns about AI infrastructure spending, and Bloom's cash consumption. The company used $27.2 million in operating cash during the quarter, while capital expenditures reached $153.5 million. With tech stocks already struggling amid a broader selloff, investors appear unwilling to overlook the financial costs of expanding production.

Promotion

Two ETFs to trade BE long or short: BEX & BEZ

And according to Roth MKM analyst Chip Moore, who ranks among the top 3% of Wall Street analysts, the latest plunge doesn't necessarily mean it's time to go bargain hunting. Moore acknowledges the company's progress but remains unwilling to recommend buying shares at current levels.

"We like the long-term opportunity and favor Bloom's position with established technology that can be rapidly deployed in markets that are increasingly grid-constrained, but valuation and lack of transparency keeps us on the sidelines," Moore explained.

Moore's hesitation comes despite growing confidence in Bloom's competitive position and commercial prospects. The analyst sees significant opportunities to serve data centers and industrial customers seeking alternatives to traditional electricity infrastructure. However, the analyst believes the stock already reflects expectations for significant future orders and manufacturing expansion, leaving little room for disappointment.

On the positive side, Moore is encouraged by Bloom's growing customer pipeline and its ability to increase production in response to rising demand. The company is working to expand its annual manufacturing capacity to 5 gigawatts, with additional facilities offering opportunities for further growth.

Still, Moore believes investors should exercise caution when considering how much future success is already reflected in Bloom's valuation.

"While we believe that Bloom's demand funnel continues to build (supported by the unprecedented pace of power growth underway and time-to-power constraints), a lack of transparency (along with a history of prior hype cycles) keeps us at Neutral," Moore summed up.

Alongside his Neutral rating, Moore lowered his 12-month price target to $230 from $260, reflecting lower valuation multiples throughout the sector. (To watch Moore's track record, click here)

Overall, Wall Street is evenly split between bulls and fence-sitters, with Bloom earning a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 10 Buys and 10 Holds. Still, the average 12-month price target of $292.72 points to a potential gain of 52% from current levels. (See BE stock forecast)

data.title: Oracle Stock (ORCL) Hit with 14% Price-Target Cut by Goldman — Here's Why
data.description:
Five-star Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges slashed her price target for Oracle shares (ORCL) by 14% on Friday, from $240 to $206. The new price target still implies about 64% upside. The analyst, who maintained her Buy rating, flagged several key concerns. These include whether Oracle's fiscal 2028-2030 targets are achievable.

Oracle Chases $166B in AI Cloud Sales by 2030

For context, Oracle has previously set a target of reaching $166 billion in cloud sales by 2030. This comes as the company's AI cloud infrastructure business continues to drive its growth. In fiscal Q1 2027, this division generated $11.6 billion in sales, up 62% from last year. This accounted for 60% of overall revenue.

What's more, Oracle's revenue grew 30% year-over-year to $19.3 billion during the quarter. The tech giant also booked over $30 billion in new AI cloud contracts. This pushed its remaining performance obligation (RPO) to $664 billion. RPO refers to contracts not yet executed.

Goldman Cuts Oracle Price Target Ahead of 2026 Investor Day

Meanwhile, Borges noted that she cut her price target as Oracle's Investor Day approaches.

Furthermore, Borges said questions remain about the progress of Oracle's data center buildout. For context, Oracle is currently working through delays to its massive Project Jupiter AI campus in New Mexico.

data.title: LKQ Stock Dives 20% on Preliminary Q3 Results and a CEO Departure
data.description:
LKQ (LKQ) stock took a nearly 20% beating on Friday after the vehicle parts distributor released its preliminary earnings results for Q3 2026. Additionally, the company revealed a leadership change.

Starting with the preliminary Q3 results, LKQ reported:

  • Revenue of $3.32 billion, compared with $3.5 billion in the third quarter of 2025.
  • A parts and services organic revenue decline of 5.4%
  • A net loss of $16 million to $32 million, including $111 million of non-cash impairment charges, compared with net income of $178 million in the third quarter of 2025
  • A diluted loss per share of 6 cents to 12 cents, including 42 cents per share in non-cash impairment charges, compared with diluted EPS of 69 cents in the third quarter of 2025
  • Adjusted diluted EPS of 47 cents to 53 cents, compared with 84 cents in the third quarter of 2025
  • Europe parts and services organic revenue decline of 9.8%.
  • Europe parts and services EBITDA margin of 4.1% to 5.1%, compared with 10% in the third quarter of 2025.

For the record, LKQ's preliminary results don't look good next to Wall Street's estimates. Its adjusted EPS midpoint of 50 cents would easily miss Wall Street's estimate of 69 cents. The same is true for its revenue of $3.32 billion when compared to analysts' estimate of $3.41 billion.
